name: UserVoice
subcategory: feedback boards, interviews and product research
tagline: Run a focused feedback portal and manual research repository

pricing.notes: Pricing is sales-led; canonical monthly amount is null.

tiers.name: Custom
tiers.limits: Unlimited seats; price varies by feedback volume, selected tools and integrations.
tiers.notes: Quote required; the vendor states it does not charge by seat.

pricing.billingTerms: Custom contract pricing only; a 30-day trial is available through sales.
pricing.hiddenCosts: Over-limit use may create additional monthly spend under the contract; professional services are available separately; typical onboarding is 4-6 weeks, with technical setup commonly 1-2 weeks.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For UserVoice, run a focused feedback portal and manual research repository. The hard boundary is enterprise customer identity, integrations, analytics, governance, and consulting, plus participant network, synthesis workflow, and collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: Collect structured feedback in a focused portal and research repository, merge duplicates, connect evidence to themes, and publish a transparent status or research view.
whatYouLose: enterprise customer identity, integrations, analytics, governance, and consulting
moatNotes: participant network, synthesis workflow, and collaboration
ongoingBurden: recruitment, consent, scheduling, media storage, transcription, tagging consistency, notifications, search, and retention
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for UserVoice because people pay either for access to participants or for a research repository that keeps evidence usable across an organization. The recurring cost buys recruitment, consent, scheduling, media storage, transcription, tagging consistency, notifications, search, and retention, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Fider
priorArt.desc: Open-source customer-feedback portal with voting and status workflows.

alternatives.name: Quackback
alternatives.desc: A focused feedback portal plus an internal evidence inbox, without UserVoice's enterprise procurement ritual.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Essentials plan and a small-team feedback repository DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for UserVoice in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Resend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: collect structured feedback in a focused portal and research repository, merge duplicates, connect evidence to themes, and publish a transparent status or research view.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create public and private feedback intake with consent text and optional contact details.
Support posts, votes, comments, tags, statuses, owners, and duplicate merging.
Add a research note type with evidence links, quotes, themes, and confidence.
Build search and filters across feedback, customers, segments, themes, and status.
Provide email notifications, moderation, export, deletion, and an audit log.
Publish a read-only roadmap or findings page using only explicitly public items.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out a paid research-participant marketplace.
Deliberately leave out unlimited video storage and automated transcription.
Deliberately leave out enterprise repositories, SSO, and governance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
